issues.summary: The fixed 60 Hz game loop is steady, but physical ProMotion scanout can still shift an otherwise complete source frame by one or more 120 Hz intervals. issues.mitigation_note: The 2026-08-30 fixed-clock change removed the measured 29-46 ms game-loop stalls. The follow-up native Metal path keeps emulation at that fixed 60 Hz and uses an independent CAMetalDisplayLink, a three-frame immutable queue, one-frame presentation lead, and two 120 Hz draws per source frame. Sharp Bilinear became the fullscreen default, with Smooth and Pixel Sharp retained as explicit choices. Three 780-frame runs remain byte-identical and the presenter reports no producer drops, consumer skips, missing source frames, backward transitions, or starvation. A clean visible sample held 8.333 ms physical intervals and 16.667 ms source transitions, but other current-build visible samples reached approximately 12 ms p99 drawable intervals and approximately 20.5 ms p99 source transitions even while the CPU loop stayed near 16.667 ms. The new dkc1.scanout.v1 trace records actual drawable presentedTime beside camera and BG1-BG3 scroll so the remaining compositor-level variability can be diagnosed without changing game state. September 6: adopted eight-observation refresh qualification with a timestamp fallback, keeping the independent fixed 60 Hz producer. The new five-minute run has zero repeat-goal changes (baseline 116 in 30 seconds), but physical scanout still varies and occluded drawables occur. This remains open; see docs/HOST_ADOPTION_IMPLEMENTATION.md.
